core.title: Drive interlocking tests through the production runners, not mocks
core.given: An end-to-end test that exercises an interlocking route or train
core.when: the test is written or changed to prove route/train behavior
core.then: Drive the production runner chain — the route-resolution runner that resolves the guarded route to exactly one selected train, then the train-execution runner that executes it — so the asserted evidence comes from the real runners, with no mock, substituted runner or hand-built resolver standing in for them.
prefer: Invoke the production route-resolution runner, constructed over the interlocking plan artifact, with guard-relevant inputs; it resolves the guarded route to exactly one selected train.
Pass that selected train to the production train-execution runner and execute it through the real execution path.
Assert the selected train and the route- or acceptance-specific result of its execution.
avoid: Mock objects standing in for either production runner (a mock route-resolution or train-execution runner).
The test framework's module-mocking idiom applied to a runner module (worst case: it swaps the entire route-control module).

Spy, stub or restore idioms of the current test framework aimed at a runner; mock idioms of a framework the suite is migrating from applied around a runner module; spy idioms of a migrating framework that replace a runner's route-resolution/execution behavior (a migrating-framework spy that only observes, without replacing behavior, is not itself forbidden).
A hand-built route resolver (a local route-resolution function or resolver class) standing in for the production route-resolution runner.
Importing the real runners only to satisfy the check while assertions come from a parallel fake path.
Asserting a plan literal without driving production route resolution and execution.
unless: Not an interlocking test: no interlocking route/train token and no production runner symbol.
core.why: A test that replaces either runner with a double exercises the double, not production route control — a descriptive green proving nothing about production.
evidence: The test references both production runners (route resolution and train execution) and contains none of the forbidden substitution patterns.
Breaking production route-resolution or train-execution behavior would make the test red.
The asserted evidence (selected train and its execution result) comes from the real runner chain.
verification: Strict disposition: a finding of this rule blocks (severity 1).

Scope: the check scans the stack's end-to-end tests (roles.e2e_test.path) that are interlocking-related — a test is interlocking-related if it references any interlocking route/train token or a production runner symbol; otherwise it is out of scope.
Check 1: an interlocking test must reference BOTH production runners — the route-resolution runner and the train-execution runner (idiom.interlocking_runners).
Check 2: any one forbidden substitution pattern — a test double replacing a production runner, enumerated by the stack's own idioms (idiom.forbidden_runner_substitutions) — is a violation.
Comments are masked before pattern matching, so a forbidden pattern that appears only inside a comment is not a violation.

Symbol reference is only a structural proxy, not sufficient semantic proof: a reviewer must confirm that the case drives the production runners with guard-relevant inputs and observes the claimed route/train behavior.
The production runner chain is the interlocking call model (design ref afokapu/atdd#1251): entry -> route resolution (guarded route to exactly one selected train) -> train execution.
Discovery scope, the comment-masking mechanics and the exact pattern list are delegated to the stack realization.

fires: An end-to-end test references an interlocking route but never references the train-execution runner.
An interlocking end-to-end test replaces a runner module with the test framework's module-mocking idiom.
An interlocking end-to-end test defines a hand-built route resolver (a local route-resolution function or resolver class) instead of driving the production route-resolution runner.
An interlocking end-to-end test uses the current test framework's spy/mock/restore idiom aimed at a runner.
An interlocking end-to-end test uses a migrating framework's spy idiom to replace runner behavior (route resolution / train execution).
doesNotFire: An end-to-end test with no interlocking route/train token and no production runner symbol.
A forbidden pattern that appears only inside a comment (comments are masked).
Interlocking tests realized in another stack, which owns its own rendering of this rule.

profileRequirements.meaning: Where the stack's end-to-end tests live; this is the discovery scope of the rule's check.

The stack's concrete symbols, entry points and full invocation shape for the two production interlocking runners — the route-resolution runner (constructed over the interlocking plan artifact, invoked with an action and inputs, resolving the guarded route to exactly one selected train) and the train-execution runner (which receives that selected train and executes it through the real runtime path) — which an interlocking test must reference and drive, including the selected-train handoff between the two runners.
profileRequirements.bunValue: InterlockingRunner and TrainRunner; call model InterlockingRunner.resolveTrain -> TrainRunner.execute; construct new InterlockingRunner(interlockingYamlPath) and call .resolveTrain(action, inputs), which resolves the guarded route to exactly one trainId; pass that trainId to the production TrainRunner and execute the selected train through the real runtime path

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's test-double idioms that count as a forbidden substitution when aimed at a production runner or its route-resolution/execution behavior, including mock classes and hand-built resolvers standing in for the route-resolution runner; a migrating-framework spy idiom counts only when it replaces runner behavior.
profileRequirements.bunValue: MockInterlockingRunner/MockTrainRunner; mock.module(...) replacing a runner module; spyOn(...)/mock(...)/mock.restore(...) aimed at a runner (bun:test); vi.mock(...)/jest.mock(...) around a runner module; vi.spyOn(...)/jest.spyOn(...) replacing runner behavior (resolveTrain/execute); a locally defined resolveTrain function or *Resolver class standing in for InterlockingRunner

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's concrete symbols, entry points and full invocation shape for the two production interlocking runners of the call model — the route-resolution runner (constructed over the interlocking plan artifact, invoked with an action and inputs, resolving the guarded route to exactly one selected train) and the train-execution runner (which receives that selected train and executes it through the real runtime path) — including the selected-train handoff between the two runners.
proposedKeys.bunValue: InterlockingRunner and TrainRunner; call model InterlockingRunner.resolveTrain -> TrainRunner.execute; construct new InterlockingRunner(interlockingYamlPath) and call .resolveTrain(action, inputs), which resolves the guarded route to exactly one trainId; pass that trainId to the production TrainRunner and execute the selected train through the real runtime path
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No idiom key names the domain runner objects of the interlocking call model; every existing idiom key describes delivery-machinery or markup constructs, while this rule needs the stack's own names and invocation shapes for the two production runners.

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's test-double idioms that count as a forbidden substitution when aimed at a production runner or its route-resolution/execution behavior, including mock classes and hand-built resolvers standing in for the route-resolution runner; a migrating-framework spy idiom counts only when it replaces runner behavior.
proposedKeys.bunValue: MockInterlockingRunner/MockTrainRunner; mock.module(...) replacing a runner module; spyOn(...)/mock(...)/mock.restore(...) aimed at a runner (bun:test); vi.mock(...)/jest.mock(...) around a runner module; vi.spyOn(...)/jest.spyOn(...) replacing runner behavior (resolveTrain/execute); a locally defined resolveTrain function or *Resolver class standing in for InterlockingRunner
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The vocabulary has no key for test-double or mocking idioms; this rule's check must enumerate the stack's substitution patterns, and no existing key (all production-code or markup constructs) fits.

bunOnly.reason: Finding and detector ids of this one rule are realization details; the core's verification names the two failure modes generically (missing production-runner reference; forbidden substitution pattern).

neutralityNotes: The domain vocabulary 'interlocking', 'route', 'train', 'guarded route' and the two-runner call model (afokapu/atdd#1251) are stack-neutral concepts of the ATDD framework itself (they appear in the rule id), so they stay in the core. What could not be made neutral: (1) the concrete runner symbols, entry points and invocation shape — constructor over the interlocking plan artifact, the (action, inputs) call resolving to exactly one selected train, and the selected-train handoff to the execution runner — carried as the proposed profile key idiom.interlocking_runners so each stack supplies its own; (2) the enumerated forbidden substitution idioms (mock.module, bun:test spyOn/mock/mock.restore, vi.mock/jest.mock, vi.spyOn/jest.spyOn only when replacing runner behavior, local resolveTrain/*Resolver) — carried as the proposed profile key idiom.forbidden_runner_substitutions; (3) the discovery glob e2e/**/*.ts — carried as roles.e2e_test.path; (4) the language fact (typescript/bun) and the detector/family/finding ids (bun_interlocking_coverage, missing_production_runner_symbol, forbidden_substitution) — bunOnly, per the notProfileKeys rule. Masking is comment-only, exactly as the Bun rewrite specifies; the mechanics of masking are delegated to the stack realization.
